title: Сценарий артхаусного фильма  (The Arthouse Movie Script)

segments.t: In the corridor, Nagiyev studies a script for an upcoming arthouse movie he desperately wants a role in. When the cooks ask what the film is about, they admit they understand nothing at all, prompting Nagiyev to dramatically describe a scene with Carlos on a raft.

Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Oh, is that you?' The grammar packs 'oh no' and 'you' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Fedya answers right away.
'It is a brand-new movie.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'the cinema' before landing on 'new'.
'I need it for a role.' The grammar packs 'for' and 'needed' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'That is what I thought.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'thought'. Senya answers right away.
'What kind of movie is it?' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'movie' in spoken Russian.
'I did not understand a single thing.' Fedya anchors the line on 'nothing', while 'understood?' completes the thought.
'Nothing whatsoever.' Notice how Russian expresses 'at all' and 'nothing' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Fedya answers right away.
'This is not our usual trash.' The grammar packs 'this' and 'junk' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Picture a waterfall.' In Russian, the idea of 'imagine' flows naturally into 'waterfall' without extra filler words.
'Carlos is lying on the edge of a raft.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Carlos' before landing on 'raft'. Senya answers right away.
'Yes, Carlos.' The grammar packs 'yes' and 'Carlos' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'A cold wind blowing from the shore.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'cold' and finishing on 'shore'.

'Which a human hand will never touch again.' Senya brings out the contrast between 'which' and 'now' in a few short words. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
